title: Henri IV to Philippe de Bethune (Rome), 9, 10 and 22 Nov 1601, BnF fr. 3484 nos. 7, 8, 12

steps.what: Volume fetched from Gallica; leaves mapped; the clear minute of 10 Nov found at f. 36 by reading the sheets.
EM alignment of the 10 Nov cipher with its minute plus the glossed passages of 8 Nov and 10 Dec gives the letter values and word signs.
10 Nov letter read in full against the minute.
9 Nov letter decoded with the key and language-model decoders: about six words in ten.
4x re-transcription fixed the doubling sign and the syllable groups 61-73.
Oracle on the known-plaintext blocks: transcription caps decoding at about 71 % of letters; decoder already at the ceiling.
Automatic glyph segmentation and template alignment.
22 Nov letter transcribed in full; clear text read, cipher runs decode to fragments only.
Full-resolution re-reading and figure-split lattice on f. 33; union of two independent readings worth about 2.9 points.
Xivrey, Melanges de Colbert 17, fr. 3677/3678 excluded; Cinq cents de Colbert 346 and Halphen's edition identified, not accessible.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 1107 tokens, 100 types, fr-1600-letters order 4: reading -2.627 per letter; polyphonic: 33% of read tokens differ from their type's commonest value. Verdict: not applicable.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): 10 Nov corpus_v2.txt + reading_10nov.md; 9 Nov ct_f33_v2.txt + decoder output decode_f33_v3/v2 (substance only); 22 Nov reading_22nov.md + ct_22nov.txt (cipher runs decoded only in fragments); key key.tsv

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test): reading_10nov.md reads (83% of sentences clean, docs/_check_reading.py, from the clear minute); decode_f33_v3.txt (9 Nov) gives broken lines with nonsense words, and the 22 Nov cipher runs are fragments ('a substance, not a reading'). 9 Nov and 22 Nov relabelled decoded, not read; fraction_read 0.55 -> ~0.2 (estimated).

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b17), step 1: Halphen, Lettres inedites du roi Henri IV a monsieur de Bethune ... du 18 octobre au 24 decembre 1601 (1889) found in full view on HathiTrust (record 100644113, item iau.31858014633857, public domain); babel.hathitrust.org answers with a Cloudflare human-verification page (curl 403; the browser pane shows the checkbox), which this session does not pass. Not on the Internet Archive, Gallica or Google Books (searched). Not on DECODE.

Re-read, step 2: no new image route or transcription; the measured transcription ceiling (oracle 71%, two readers agree on 69% of glyphs, third pass) stands, so the 9 Nov and 22 Nov decodes stay fragments. Both kept decoded, not read; the edition is the route.

Consistency pass (cl): 'read in part' not justified: the Halphen 1889 gap is genuinely untried (not-attempted kept) and the print, key-rebuild and retry escalation steps are not done (left unticked); NOTES Status: in progress. The umbrella gap line for the 9 and 22 Nov runs restated as a lead sentence (its two letters are separate gap lines, mirrored in outcome.gaps).

About 750 of 3,600, estimated. The earlier 0.55 (NOTES prose) is withdrawn as a reading figure.
outcome.notes: 10 Nov read in full; 9 Nov about six words in ten; 22 Nov clear text read, cipher in fragments. Open code groups include 44, 45, 62, 66-72, 26-28, 5, 3, 8. fraction_read estimated from the notes (10 Nov full; 9 Nov about half the words; 22 Nov clear text read, cipher runs fragments only), not measured. codes_open counts the 19 code numbers listed open in NOTES (2, 5, 6, 8, 9, 12, 20, 26-28, 31, 44, 45, 62, 66, 67, 69, 72, 80); total not counted. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: 9 Nov and 22 Nov letters relabelled decoded, not read; only the 10 Nov letter reads.

texts.label: 10 Nov 1601, f. 34r-v
texts.summary: Henri IV tells Béthune that he paid Cardinal Aldobrandini 10,000 écus through Sillery as a gratification after the Parlement's judgment in the Este-Aldobrandini debt, and will pay 10,000 more in the first months of 1602; Béthune is to tell the Cardinal through Cardinal d'Ossat and pretend not to have received the letter. The cipher is entries A to V3 of corpus_v2.txt (the other entries are glossed passages of the 8 Nov and 10 Dec letters); the text comes from the clear minute on f. 36.

reading_review.note: The four cipher passages read from the clear minute f. 36r-v, which gives their full text; continuous French.

texts.note: Re-read 22-23 Oct 2026 (b17), still decoded, not read: no DECODE record; no decipherment on or near f. 33 (leaf map, NOTES); the decode stays at the measured transcription ceiling (oracle 71% of letters on known blocks; two careful readings of the hand agree on 69% of glyphs), so its lines do not build sentences ('mil escus et la cetresioatl depentionrln sur le reuenu de naples'). Blockers: illegible (the glyph families g/looped g, m/hooked m, r/2-shaped r differ by a hook at the 450 dpi of the only images) and a clear text not yet consulted: Halphen, Lettres inedites du roi Henri IV a M. de Bethune (1889), is in full view on HathiTrust (iau.31858014633857) but behind a human-verification page this session must not pass; BnF Cinq cents de Colbert 346 (copy register Aug 1601-Nov 1602) is not digitised.
texts.label: 9 Nov 1601, f. 33r
texts.summary: A page entirely in cipher about the Spanish news from La Rochepot's secretary and the cardinalate of Don Alexandre, with the cardinals of Joyeuse and d'Ossat. The decryption is decoder output only (about six words in ten); bracketed numbers are open code groups.

texts.note: Re-read 22-23 Oct 2026 (b17), still decoded, not read: the clear French reads (reading_22nov.md) but its 80 cipher runs, most of the letter, decode only to fragments at the transcription ceiling measured for this hand; no decipherment on the leaves (ff. 45, 48 are address leaves). Blockers as for 9 Nov: illegible glyph families at the images' resolution, and the clear texts in Halphen 1889 (HathiTrust iau.31858014633857, full view behind human verification, not opened here) and BnF Cinq cents de Colbert 346 (not digitised).
texts.label: 22 Nov 1601, ff. 46r-47v
texts.summary: Saint-Germain-en-Laye, answering Béthune's despatch of 29 October: a rebuke of two persons named by code groups for not breaking 'ce coup', the pension of Camaiano to raise the French party in Rome, the Pope's welcome, Barberini's coming, and the baptism of the Dauphin. The clear text is transcribed in full; the 80 cipher runs decode only to fragments.

prior.where: Clear minute of the 10 Nov letter (f. 36) and marginal glosses of other letters in the same volume; none for 9 or 22 Nov
